Moss developer Polyarc has shut down
The Seattle-based VR specialist has closed its doors after over a decade.
Chris Kerr
,
Senior Editor, News
,
GameDeveloper.com
September 14, 2026
schedule
1 Min Read
Image via Polyarc
Seattle-based VR specialist Polyarc has folded after over a decade. The company was best known for developing the Moss franchise, which began life a a VR series before eventually being reimagined for more traditional platforms.
The studio confirmed its closure in a
brief post on LinkedIn
. It's unclear how many people have lost their jobs as a result of the shutdown—although a
reverse recruiting tracker
shared by the studio indicates that almost 30 people have been let go.
That might, however, include some of the people
laid off earlier this year
—with Polyarc choosing to significantly downsize in March 2026 after due to financing challenges.
"Today is the end of an era for Polyarc. After nearly 12 years riding the joyous rollercoaster of emotions that is making video games, our time together has come to an end. As we wind down active development, we are saying our farewells to each other," reads the post.
Related:
Worker-run studio KO_OP confirms layoffs
"Working together over all of these years has been an honor. Bringing surprise and delight to those who played our games has been a privilege. Thank you to everyone at Polyarc, our work is now finished."
